Gallery copies
Use Google Photos’ Free up space feature to remove copies it considers safely backed up. This does not remove PhotoBridge originals.

Original files
Export an original archive to external storage, then confirm reclamation after verification. An archive saved on this phone still uses its space.

Optional relay mode reclaims private originals after a saved gallery copy is verified. This does not verify Google Photos cloud backup or preserve the original format of converted motion/burst files.

About usage
File sizes exclude database, cache and filesystem overhead. Gallery usage covers this installation’s PhotoBridge album files, excludes trash and may lag changes to the media index. This does not verify cloud backup.
Reclaim originals after saving to gallery
Off: keep original files. On: while reception is running, verify gallery copies and reclaim matching staging originals. Missing or changed copies keep their originals.
Use this device as a relay?

PhotoBridge will reopen and verify each saved gallery copy before reclaiming its private originals, including eligible existing items. Transfer receipts remain.

This confirms storage in the phone gallery, not Google Photos cloud backup. Motion and burst photos can use converted formats; their original components will no longer be available from this device. Keep your source library or another original backup. Older converted copies without verification records keep their originals.

You can turn this off at any time. Reclaimed originals are not restored by turning it off.
Relay enabled. Originals will be checked while reception runs.

Optional features being evaluated. Each has its own controls and explanation.
Free device space using Google Photos, with optional automatic cleanup.

1. Enable “Google Photos space management” in Android Accessibility settings.
2. Start the 2-minute check.
3. In Google Photos, open your profile, then “Free up space on this device”. Stop before the final Free up button.
4. Return here to see the result.
The read-only check never clicks or deletes. Automatic cleanup requires separate consent and account binding. PhotoBridge originals and gallery copies use separate retention rules.

PhotoBridge uses Android Accessibility to read selected on-screen controls in Google Photos only during a check you start, for up to 2 minutes. This includes the Free up space message and buttons. Account descriptions, photo labels and screenshots are not collected. Page text is processed in memory on this device; only result categories are kept in memory or included when you export a report. Nothing is sent to a server. No clicks or deletions are performed. You can stop a check here or disable this service in Android Settings.
Read Google Photos controls for checks. With separate opt-in, navigate and free safely backed-up device copies.

Find the steps for your current task. These pages remain available while receiving is stopped.
Pair a phone or computer and check the local network.
Understand background reception, restarts and sender scheduling.
Received originals, gallery copies and cloud backup are separate steps.
Choose how to retain originals and make room for new transfers.
Retry processing, export diagnostics and preserve data during updates.

Connect both devices to the same reachable local network and start receiving here. On an iPhone, scan the code displayed by this receiver. On a Mac, display a computer pairing code and scan it with this receiver. Camera permission is needed only for scanning. Check the device names after pairing; renaming a device keeps its existing identity and receipts.

The current Android receiver requires Wi-Fi with an IPv4 address. Guest networks, client isolation and some VPN routes can prevent devices from reaching each other even when they show the same network name. Return to the original local network and retry. A Wi-Fi interruption is retried automatically while receiving remains enabled.

The receiver keeps its identity and received files when its Wi-Fi address changes. Updated Apple senders discover the new local address and verify it using the existing pairing before reconnecting. Open the sender to allow discovery; a manually paused backup stays paused. If the network blocks discovery, scan a new pairing code. Keep both apps updated. Do not clear app data to reconnect.

Start receiving before leaving PhotoBridge. Android runs the receiver as a foreground service and may show an ongoing notification; allow notifications when requested. If your phone restricts background activity, check its battery settings. Stopping reception explicitly prevents automatic restoration until you start it again.
After a restart or system stop

Settings → Receiving controls restoration after restart. On Android 15 or later, this app asks you to open PhotoBridge to resume instead of starting reception at boot. The system can also limit long-running background work. Return to the app and start receiving if prompted; existing receipts and partial transfers are retained.
The sender also needs time to run

A ready receiver cannot force a sender to run. iOS decides when background preparation and requests can continue; uninterrupted locked-screen backup is not guaranteed. Keep the sender open for an initial large import, and reopen it if work stalls. A Mac sender needs the app running and the computer awake.

PhotoBridge confirms receipt only after all resources for an item arrive and pass integrity checks. A motion photo can contain an original still image and a paired video under one logical item. A processing failure after receipt does not require uploading those originals again.
Published means a device-gallery copy exists

The receiver prepares a system-gallery copy after receipt, including supported Motion Photo conversion and burst metadata. Check Transfers for processing status and retry failed processing there. Grouped burst display in an external gallery depends on that gallery; source originals and per-frame receipts remain separate.
Cloud backup is a separate operation

Google Photos performs its own upload. Select the intended account and enable backup for the PhotoBridge device folder if needed. A PhotoBridge receipt or gallery publication does not confirm cloud backup. The current experiment only checks recognizable Google Photos screens; it does not delete files or enable automatic cleanup.

Storage limits includes an original-storage budget and a minimum free-space reserve. Gallery copies and conversion scratch files also occupy the phone. Increasing the original budget does not create free disk space. If space is insufficient, review the separate original and gallery totals before choosing what to retain.

Originals are retained by default. Export a verified original archive to external storage before choosing to reclaim its eligible originals. An archive saved on this phone still occupies space. Google Photos free-up-space removes eligible system-gallery copies, not PhotoBridge private originals.

When you explicitly enable relay mode in Storage, PhotoBridge verifies the completed gallery copy before reclaiming eligible staging originals. Missing, changed or unverified copies keep their originals. A converted motion copy is not a byte-for-byte archive of its original image/video pair. Turning relay off stops new reclamation; it cannot restore already reclaimed originals. This policy does not verify cloud backup.

For a sender upload failure, inspect the sender queue and its retry controls. If originals are already received but gallery processing failed, filter Transfers for failed processing and use Retry failed processing. Space-related processing waits are checked again automatically while receiving is active. Repeated re-imports are not a substitute for resolving the underlying error.

Open Settings → Diagnostics → Export logs. Include the time of the issue and whether the sender or receiver was in the foreground. Reports contain bounded event records such as stages, task identifiers and byte counts; they do not include photo content or pairing credentials. Review a report before sharing it. The experimental screen check has its own Export check result action.

Install a newer package from the same trusted source over the existing app. If Android reports an incompatible signature, stop and obtain the matching package instead of uninstalling or clearing storage. Export important originals first if you plan to remove the app; uninstalling can remove its private data. Current builds are development previews, and there is no automatic Android update channel yet.

Let Google Photos remove device copies that it confirms are backed up. Only this receiver needs setup.
Automatically clean up when space is low
First check Google Photos on this device. This only resumes PhotoBridge transfers; it does not delete anything or certify cloud backup. Automatic cleanup will wait 15 minutes before another attempt.
Starts below %1$s available. New transfers pause during cleanup and resume under the normal storage reserve. The screen must be unlocked.
Start the receiver to read its storage threshold.

PhotoBridge uses Android Accessibility to navigate Google Photos and press Free up space only when its official message confirms these items are safely backed up. This may include backed-up device photos from other apps, not only PhotoBridge. It never presses Delete or empties cloud trash. The selected account is read in memory and only its fingerprint is saved locally. No account text, screenshots or photo labels are stored or sent. Cleanup is off by default; bind an account, then enable automation or start one cleanup. Each run is limited to 5 minutes. You can stop here or disable the accessibility service in Android Settings. An uncertain cleanup is checked without pressing Free up again. During cleanup, PhotoBridge may wake the screen and dismiss a lock screen without a PIN, password or pattern. Secure lock screens require manual unlocking.
Bind an account to get started.

Pause new transfers from this sender. Pairing and received files remain, and you can enable reception again. This is a reception control for identified clients, not a credential revocation. Older unidentified transfers are listed separately.
